objections.claim: The no-listener oracle is internally unsatisfiable as specified. Section 1 requires every spawned executable to be a repo-tracked script recursively governed by the closed grammar, but the required CLI paths explicitly depend on spawning external executables including git (`git cat-file`, history/bundle operations) and bwrap (mandatory oracle confinement), with `gh` also used for attestation verification. Under the stated grammar those commands must be rejected, so `pylae doctor` and `pylae verify --full` cannot satisfy their acceptance criteria. Merely allowing these binaries would create an unanalyzed escape from the claimed complete executable closure. The approach must define a capability-scoped external-tool exception mechanism—identity/version or digest pinning plus closed subcommand/argument/environment grammars that exclude listener-capable modes—and add regressions proving the required git/bwrap/gh invocations pass while server-mode, config/alias injection, wrapper substitution, and arbitrary-command invocations fail closed.
